chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performs Hajj on behalf of another; does that suffice for him for the Hajj of Islam? He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Is the Hajj of the Jamal (the one who pays) complete or incomplete?' He said, 'Complete.' I said, 'Is the Hajj of the Ajir (the hired agent) complete or incomplete?' He said, 'Complete.'
And that which indicates that Hajj is obligatory upon him when he becomes wealthy is what has been narrated:

key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْأَجِيرِ: The Hajj of the hired agent (one who performs the ritual)
key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْجَمَّالِ: The Hajj of the payer (one who provides the funds)

ai.seo_question: Does Hajj performed by a hired agent count as complete for the person who paid for it?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that Hajj performed on behalf of another (Hajj al-Nawab) fully discharges the original obligation of Islam, regardless of whether the agent is a relative or a hired worker. This ruling underscores the Shia view that the validity of the substitute's performance is not diminished by the nature of the relationship or compensation, provided the agent performs it correctly. It highlights the theological principle that the spiritual reward and legal discharge transfer to the principal, reinforcing the communal and familial dimensions of religious duty in Shia jurisprudence.
